title: Pet Vaccinations: A Practical Guide for Bangladeshi Pet Families
excerpt: Vaccines protect pets from preventable diseases. This guide explains what to ask your vet, how to build a schedule, and what to expect after vaccination.
content:
Vaccinations are one of the most effective ways to protect pets from serious illness.

What to discuss with your vet:
- Your pet’s age and past vaccination records
- Lifestyle (indoor/outdoor, travel, boarding, multi-pet homes)
- Local risk factors (disease prevalence, stray animal exposure)

Typical process:
1) Health check
2) Vaccine administration
3) Observation for a short period
4) Follow-up schedule planning

Aftercare:
- Mild tiredness or decreased appetite can happen for a day
- Watch for swelling, vomiting, severe lethargy, or breathing difficulty and contact your vet immediately

If you don’t have records, your vet can help plan a safe restart schedule.

This content is educational and not a substitute for professional veterinary advice.

title: Healthy Pet Diet Basics: What to Feed and What to Avoid
excerpt: A balanced diet supports energy, skin and coat health, digestion, and long-term wellbeing. Learn the basics of choosing safe food for dogs and cats.
content:
A healthy diet depends on species, age, activity level, and medical history.

Core principles:
- Choose complete and balanced food for the correct life stage
- Measure portions to prevent obesity
- Provide fresh clean water at all times

Common foods to avoid:
- Chocolate, grapes/raisins, onions/garlic
- Excess salty foods
- Cooked bones (splinter risk)

If your pet has allergies, sensitive digestion, or chronic disease, consult a vet before changing diet.

This content is educational and not a substitute for professional veterinary advice.

title: Hot Weather Pet Care: How to Keep Your Pet Hydrated and Safe
excerpt: Heat stress can be dangerous. Here’s how to reduce risk, encourage hydration, and spot early warning signs in hot Bangladeshi weather.
content:
In hot weather, pets can overheat quickly.

Hydration tips:
- Keep water bowls in multiple rooms
- Refresh water frequently
- Offer ice cubes (if your pet tolerates them)

Safety tips:
- Avoid midday walks; choose early morning or evening
- Provide shade and ventilation
- Never leave pets in parked vehicles

Warning signs of heat stress:
- Heavy panting, drooling
- Weakness, vomiting
- Bright red gums or collapse

If you suspect heat stress, move the pet to a cool area and contact a vet immediately.
